digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store healing and multi-bundle reconciliation
propositions: When multiple bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.

git-remote-s3's push helper rejects all ref operations while len(bundles) > 1 before writing anything, and rebar's non-fast-forward retry cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, causing push stalls that never converge.

Upstream's git-s3 doctor is interactive-only (blocks on input() at EOF in autonomous fleets) and discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs, causing irreversible loss of unique ticket events from an append-only event log.

The S3 multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at the bundle-storage layer and can be resolved by lossless 2-parent merges using rebar's existing sync reconciliation semantics, never discarding any head.

The heal must write a merged bundle before deleting any original bundles and never delete the merged result, guaranteeing at least one lossless bundle remains at every crash point for recovery on the next run.

Concurrent repairs against a shared remote must serialize via the helper's per-ref lock (acquire_lock/release_lock with TTL/steal), with exactly one doctor performing the merge while others back off and converge on the winner's collapsed state.
